novel.definition: A printed and bound book that is an extended work of fiction.

comic-book.definition: A book or magazine that tells stories mainly through sequences of drawings and speech or caption text.
comic-book.exampleUsage: He borrowed a comic book from the library.

magazine.definition: A thin publication with articles and pictures, released regularly.

newspaper.definition: A daily or weekly publication on folded sheets.

journal.definition: A record book as a physical object.

diary.definition: A personal journal (as a physical object).

poetry.definition: Writing arranged to express ideas or feelings through rhythm and carefully chosen words.

blog.definition: A shared on-line journal where people can post diary entries about their personal experiences and hobbies.

e-reader.definition: A portable electronic device designed mainly for reading digital books and documents.
e-reader.exampleUsage: She read a novel on her e-reader.

audiobook.definition: A recording of a book being read aloud.

drawing.definition: An illustration that is drawn by hand and published in a book, magazine, or newspaper.

painting.definition: A picture made with paint and shown on a wall.

sculpting.definition: The art or activity of shaping materials such as clay, wax, wood, or stone into three-dimensional forms.
sculpting.exampleUsage: The class practiced sculpting with soft clay.

origami.definition: The Japanese art of folding paper into shapes representing objects (e.g., flowers or birds).
origami.exampleUsage: The origami was identified during the lesson.

scrapbooking.definition: The hobby of arranging photographs, notes, and decorative materials in an album.
scrapbooking.exampleUsage: She used scrapbooking to preserve travel photos.

calligraphy.definition: The art of making decorative, carefully formed handwriting.

pottery.definition: Ceramic ware made from clay and baked in a kiln.

mosaic.definition: A picture or design made from small pieces of colored material.

collage.definition: A paste-up made by sticking together pieces of paper or photographs to form an artistic image.

decoupage.definition: Art produced by decorating a surface with cutouts and then coating it with several layers of varnish or lacquer.

guitar.definition: A stringed instrument usually having six strings.
guitar.exampleUsage: The guitar was used during the activity.

piano.definition: (used chiefly as a direction or description in music) soft.

drums.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Drums" in an educational description.
drums.definition: Percussion instruments played by striking stretched surfaces.

violin.definition: Bowed stringed instrument that is the highest member of the violin family.
violin.exampleUsage: The violin was used during the activity.

flute.exampleUsage: The flute was used during the activity.

ukulele.definition: A small guitar having four strings.

harmonica.definition: A small rectangular free-reed instrument having a row of free reeds set back in air holes and played by blowing into the desired hole.
harmonica.exampleUsage: The harmonica was used during the activity.

keyboard.definition: Device consisting of a set of keys on a piano or organ or typewriter or typesetting machine or computer or the like.
keyboard.exampleUsage: The keyboard was used during the activity.

saxophone.definition: A single-reed woodwind with a conical bore.

cello.exampleUsage: The cello was used during the activity.

stamps.definition: Small printed labels used to pay for sending mail, often collected as a hobby.

coins.definition: Metal pieces used as money, sometimes collected as a hobby.

cards.definition: A game played with playing cards.

figurines.definition: A small carved or molded figure.

vinyl-records.definition: Flat grooved discs that store recorded sound in an analog format and are played on a turntable.
vinyl-records.exampleUsage: The music room has a collection of vinyl records.

antiques.definition: Old objects valued for their age, design, or history.

shells.definition: The hard outer coverings of sea animals, often collected from beaches.

rocks.definition: Pieces of natural solid material from the ground.

comics.definition: Stories told through pictures and written dialogue.

miniatures.definition: Very small models of people, objects, or buildings.
